ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a page of a calendar, the date displayed is September 23, 2011, Friday; the text at the bottom of the calendar says “Today is the autumnal equinox (Beijing time 17:05)”. Then reason: the question asks for the geographic coordinates of the direct solar point when the autumnal equinox phenomenon occurs. Beijing time uses the local time of 120°E as the standard time. The local time of the longitude where the direct solar point is located is 12:00, while the time of the autumnal equinox given in the figure is Beijing time 17:05, which is 5 hours 05 minutes later than 12:00. The earth rotates 15° per hour, so the longitude difference is 5 hours 05 minutes × 15°/hour = 76°15′. The 120°E corresponding to Beijing time is later than the local time of the longitude where the direct solar point is located, indicating that 120°E is east of the direct-point longitude, therefore the direct-point longitude is 120°E − 76°15′ = 43°45′E. On the autumnal equinox, the sun directly shines on the equator, so the latitude is 0°. Therefore the coordinates are 43°45′E, 0°.
